back: The quantity consumers are willing and able to buy at each price in a given period.
The quantity producers are willing and able to offer for sale at each price in a given period.
The price at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied.
A change in the price of the good moves along the curve; a change in any other factor shifts the curve.
Income, prices of substitutes and complements, tastes, population, advertising, expectations and seasons.
Costs, technology, weather, taxes and subsidies, number of firms, prices of other goods and expectations.
Above equilibrium: surplus, price falls. Below equilibrium: shortage, price rises.
Demand up: price and quantity up. Supply up: price down, quantity up. Opposite for decreases.
Demand for a good because it is needed to make another good, e.g. flour for bread.
